message.content:
Based on my search, here is information about how to make federal tax payments online:

## Main Options for Paying Federal Taxes Online

### 1. IRS Direct Pay (Free)
- **Website**: Available through the IRS website
- **Cost**: Free
- **Features**:
  - Pay directly from your U.S. checking or savings account
  - No registration required
  - Schedule payments up to 365 days in advance
  - Modify or cancel payments up to two business days before the scheduled date
  - Available Monday through Saturday, midnight to 11:45 p.m. EST; Sunday 7 a.m. to 11:45 p.m. EST
  - Receive email notifications about your payment

### 2. Electronic Federal Tax Payment System (EFTPS)
- **Website**: www.eftps.gov
- **Cost**: Free
- **Features**:
  - Available 24/7
  - Schedule payments up to a year in advance
  - Access payment history for up to 16 months
  - Make payments online or by phone
  - Suitable for individuals, businesses, and tax professionals
  - **Note**: EFTPS no longer accepts new users; existing users are being transitioned to use IRS accounts or Direct Pay

### 3. IRS Online Account
- Allows you to manage and make payments through your personal IRS account

### 4. Debit Card, Credit Card, or Digital Wallet
- **Processors**: Pay1040 or ACI Payments
- **Cost**: 
  - Debit card: ~$2.10-$2.15 flat fee
  - Credit card: 1.75%-1.85% of payment amount (minimum $2.50)
- **Features**:
  - Can pay online or by phone
  - Accepts various card types and digital wallets (Venmo, PayPal, Click to Pay)
  - Fees go to the processor, not the IRS

### 5. IRS2Go Mobile App
- **Cost**: Free app; card fees apply if using debit/credit
- **Features**:
  - Make payments via mobile version of IRS Direct Pay (free)
  - Pay with debit or credit card (with processing fees)
  - No registration required
  - Also helps find free tax software and tax help

### 6. Electronic Funds Withdrawal (EFW)
- Available when e-filing through tax software or with a tax professional
- **Cost**: Free (check with bank for any fees)
- Authorizes direct debit from your bank account when you file

## Important Recent Update

As of March 25, 2025, Executive Order 14247 requires that **federal tax payments must be made electronically**. Paper checks and money orders will no longer be accepted after September 30, 2025. This applies to:
- Tax payments
- Federal estimated taxes
- Federal tax refunds (must be via direct deposit or electronic method)

**Exceptions** apply for individuals without banking access, those in emergency situations, or other legally exempt cases.

## Steps to Pay Online (Using IRS Direct Pay)
1. Visit the IRS website and select "Make a Payment"
2. Choose "IRS Direct Pay"
3. Select your payment reason (e.g., 1040 balance due, estimated tax, extension)
4. Verify your identity using information from a prior-year tax return (SSN, address, date of birth, filing status)
5. Enter your bank account information
6. Schedule or submit your payment
7. Save your confirmation number

Sources:
1. https://fiscal.treasury.gov/payments-to-government/electronic-federal-tax-payment-system-eftps
2. https://www.nerdwallet.com/taxes/learn/pay-irs-options
3. https://www.zinnerco.com/zinner-blog/executive-order-requires-electronic-payment-of-federal-tax
4. https://www.taxact.com/support/1142/2020/eftps-online-electronic-federal-tax-payment-system
5. https://www.hrblock.com/tax-payment-center/
6. https://www.aggarwalcpa.com/blog/the-electronic-federal-tax-payment-system
7. https://www.wallstreetmojo.com/electronic-federal-tax-payment-system/
